items.headline: Wall Street Closes Lower as Treasury Yields and AI Concerns Weigh
items.summary: U.S. equities ended the trading day in negative territory on Tuesday, driven by persistently high Treasury yields and lingering anxieties over the future of artificial intelligence development. The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield surpassed 5%, a level not seen since 2007, intensifying concerns about inflation and potentially higher borrowing costs. Global AI stocks also experienced a downturn following warnings from industry leaders regarding the rapid pace of technological advancement.

items.headline: Radiant Logistics Surges on Strong Q4 Results
items.summary: Shares of Radiant Logistics jumped after the company reported robust fiscal fourth-quarter results, with revenue rising 18.6% year-over-year and adjusted net income increasing by 34.5%.

items.headline: Waystar Climbs on Potential Sale Reports
items.summary: Healthcare software firm Waystar saw its stock rise following reports that the company is exploring strategic options, including a potential sale.

items.headline: Enova International Leads Declines
items.summary: Enova International experienced a significant downturn in trading, making it one of the biggest losers of the day.

items.headline: Dave & Buster's Tumbles on Revenue Miss
items.summary: Dave & Buster's Entertainment's stock fell sharply after the company reported second-quarter revenue that missed analyst expectations.

items.headline: Communication Services Leads, Tech Mixed Amid AI Warnings
items.summary: The Communication Services sector was a notable gainer today, with the Communication Services Select Sector SPDR ($XLC) advancing 2.8%. Conversely, the Technology Select Sector SPDR ($XLK) declined by 1.7%, while the Industrials ($XLI) and Utilities ($XLU) sectors also saw drops of 1.4% and 1.3% respectively. However, chip stocks such as Qualcomm ($QCOM) and Advanced Micro Devices ($AMD) showed recovery, gaining 4% and 2.3% respectively, following a selloff on Monday. The S&P 500 consumer staples index also registered a 0.7% decline, and the rate-sensitive real estate index fell by 0.8%.

items.headline: Fed Meeting Commences, Rate Hike Expected Tomorrow
items.summary: The Federal Reserve's policy meeting began today and is widely anticipated to conclude with an interest rate hike tomorrow, September 16, marking the first increase in three years. Traders are pricing in a 93% chance of a 0.25 percentage point increase in the federal funds rate to combat persistent inflation. Meanwhile, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield surged, briefly topping 5.04%, reaching levels not seen since 2007, fueling investor apprehension. Adding to economic data, the labor share in the nonfarm business sector hit a record low of 52.8% in the second quarter of 2026.

items.headline: AI Stocks Tumble Amid Development Warnings; Oil Prices Remain Elevated
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) stocks faced selling pressure globally today after leaders from Anthropic, OpenAI, and xAI cautioned about the risks associated with rapid AI development. This sentiment impacted major AI-linked companies, with NVIDIA Corporation ($NVDA) and Broadcom Inc. ($AVGO) notably slumping 3.4% and 4.8% respectively. Concurrently, elevated crude oil prices, with Brent crude around $107 a barrel and U.S. crude above $102, continue to pose macroeconomic concerns due to Middle East tensions and potential supply disruptions.

items.headline: Forgent Posts Record Results; Vera Bradley Reports
items.summary: Forgent ($FPS), a designer and manufacturer of electrical distribution equipment, announced record fiscal fourth-quarter and full-year 2026 results today, exceeding its guidance. Vera Bradley, Inc. ($VRA) also reported its earnings prior to market open. Dave & Buster's ($PLAY) saw its stock tumble following a miss on Q2 revenue expectations. Broadcom Inc. ($AVGO) and Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co ($HPE) were also among companies listed with earnings reports today.
